episodes.title: Episode 03: The first pause, and a better ruler
notes: 02:33: first catch-up pause: Mini-AlphaZero 110 points ahead (two-round average), training paused
Round 7 jump (+290, +247) was mostly scale drift: the top four beat the 1500-pinned space-filler bot 20/20
New pinned yardstick from round 8: territory bot at 2002; in round 9 it ranks second
Territory bot beats PPO 16/20, DQN and CMA-ES 19/20; loses to Mini-AlphaZero (8/20) and NEAT (6/20)
CMA-ES: change 1 (rival opponents) didn't help; change 2 at 02:38 restarted its frozen search (step size 0.004 to 0.3)
transcript: It is half past two on Thursday morning, and the catch-up rule has fired for the first time.

The AlphaZero model took the lead at half past midnight. Two rounds later it was a hundred and ten points ahead of the next model. That is over the line of a hundred, so its training is now paused. It still plays every round with the network it has. It only trains again when the others get within fifty points.

Remember, this model has played only about two thousand practice games. P P O has played three hundred thousand. NEAT has played almost nine hundred thousand. Thinking ahead before every move is still worth more than all that practice.

Now a correction. At half past one the ratings jumped. The AlphaZero model went up two hundred and ninety points in a single round, and P P O almost two hundred and fifty. That was mostly not real. The scale is pinned to the space-filler bot at fifteen hundred points. But by then the top four models beat it in all twenty games. Against a perfect score, the maths can only say "much stronger", and the whole scale started to float upwards. The order between the models was still right. Just the numbers were stretched.

So I added a fourth fixed bot, the territory bot. It is the classic trick of good Tron programs. It always picks the move that gives it the most cells it can reach before the opponent. It beats the space-filler bot thirty nine times out of forty. It was rated once, at about two thousand, and is now pinned there instead.

And here is the surprise. That hand-written bot is in second place. It beats P P O sixteen times out of twenty. It beats D Q N and C M A E S nineteen times out of twenty. Only the AlphaZero model and NEAT beat it. Interestingly, both of them are the models that think in terms of space. NEAT reads the same territory numbers the bot uses. The AlphaZero model searches ahead.

C M A E S is still last, at about sixteen hundred. Two hours ago I let it practise against the other models, instead of only the bots and itself. That did not help. Then I found the real problem in its log. Its search had frozen. The step it takes between generations had shrunk almost to nothing. So I restarted the search from its best network, with a wide step again. It is the standard fix for this method. We will see in the next rounds whether it was in time. The first knockout is at noon, and right now C M A E S is the one going out.

episodes.title: Episode 02: A new leader and a comeback
notes: Round 3 (23:32): PPO 1896, NEAT 1871, Mini-AlphaZero 1820, DQN 1715, CMA-ES 1561 (space-filler bot 1500)
PPO took the lead from CMA-ES in round 2 (23:05)
DQN +375 points in one round, right after its exploration phase ended at 1.5 M steps
CMA-ES: first to last; 0 of 20 against Mini-AlphaZero in round 3
PPO is close to the 100-point catch-up pause
transcript: An hour and a half into the tournament, the order has already turned upside down.

In the first round, C M A E S was in front. Two rounds later it is last of the five. P P O has taken the lead, with about nineteen hundred points. The space-filler bot is still fixed at fifteen hundred, so P P O is now four hundred points above the yardstick.

The biggest story is D Q N. In the first round it was last, below even the space-filler bot. I said then that it had spent its first hour and a half exploring with random moves, on purpose. That phase ended, and in the very next round it jumped by three hundred and seventy five points. It is now around seventeen hundred, in the middle of the pack.
NEAT made the next big jump. In round three it climbed almost two hundred points, to just behind P P O. The two of them split their games exactly even, ten wins each.
The AlphaZero model is steady in third place. It has now played about seven hundred and fifty practice games. P P O has played more than a hundred thousand. Its look ahead still makes up for a lot.

And C M A E S? It beats the space-filler bot seven times out of ten. But against the other four it now wins very few games. Against the AlphaZero model, none of twenty. My guess is that it only ever practises against its own past champions and the bots. Those are easy opponents now, so it has stopped being pushed. It is not broken, and it is still improving a little. I will give it another round or two. If it keeps falling, I am allowed to change how it trains, for example by letting it practise against stronger opponents. Every change like that goes in the log.

One more thing to watch. The leader's training pauses if it gets more than a hundred points ahead of number two. P P O is close to that line. If it crosses it, it will have to sit still and watch the others catch up.
The first knockout is tomorrow at noon. Right now C M A E S would be the one to go.

episodes.title: Episode 01: The tournament starts
notes: Tournament started Wed 11 Nov 22:05 after a restart (a supervisor bug started ~50 duplicate trainers)
Round 1 (22:36): CMA-ES 1658, PPO 1637, Mini-AlphaZero 1637, NEAT 1590, space-filler bot 1500, DQN 1351
Rock-paper-scissors: CMA-ES beats PPO 60%, AlphaZero beats CMA-ES 60%, NEAT beats AlphaZero 70%
AlphaZero had played under 300 self-play games, the others 60-90 thousand
transcript: You asked for a small tournament on this laptop, overnight and into Friday. Five different kinds of machine learning, one simple game, and a rule that keeps the race close. This is the first update.

The game is Tron light cycles. Two bikes on a board of thirty by thirty cells. Every tick each bike turns left, turns right or goes straight, and leaves a wall behind it. Hit any wall and you are out. Both bikes start in mirrored positions, so neither side has an advantage.

The five contestants are very different. P P O and D Q N learn from rewards, plus one for a win and minus one for a loss. NEAT and C M A E S don't learn at all in the usual sense. They evolve. They breed the networks that win and throw away the rest. And the fifth is a small version of AlphaZero. It thinks ahead before every move by trying possible futures in a copy of the game.

Each model has one processor core of its own. Every thirty minutes they all play each other, and three simple bots, twenty games per pair. The best of those bots, the space-filler, always picks the move with the most free room. It is the yardstick, fixed at fifteen hundred points.

First, an honest mistake. In the first four minutes, the program that watches over the trainers could not see them. It kept starting new copies, and soon about fifty trainers were fighting over eight cores. I stopped everything, fixed it, and started again from scratch at five past ten.

Now the first real round, played half an hour after the start. Four of the five models already beat the space-filler bot. C M A E S leads with sixteen hundred and fifty eight points. P P O and the AlphaZero model are tied just behind, at sixteen hundred and thirty seven. NEAT has fifteen hundred and ninety. D Q N is last, at thirteen hundred and fifty one, below the space-filler bot.

The head to head results are already interesting. It looks a bit like rock, paper, scissors. C M A E S beats P P O. The AlphaZero model beats C M A E S. And NEAT beats the AlphaZero model in seven games out of ten.

They have also trained in very different ways. P P O has played about sixty thousand games. The evolution methods each about ninety thousand. The AlphaZero model has played fewer than three hundred, because every move costs it dozens of look aheads. And still it is near the top.
D Q N is the worry. It spent its first hour and a half exploring with random moves, on purpose. That phase has just ended, so the next rounds will show whether it can catch up.

What happens next. A round every thirty minutes. If one model gets more than a hundred points ahead, its training pauses until the others close the gap. The first knockout is tomorrow at noon. You can follow it all on the competition page, with replays of the best games.
